national.title: How to Register a Marriage in India (2026)
national.summary: Step-by-step guide to legal marriage registration under the Hindu Marriage Act or Special Marriage Act on state registration portals. Verified statutory fees of ₹5 to ₹100, witness criteria, and document requirements.

steps.title: Verify Age Eligibility and Applicable Marriage Act
steps.description: Ensure the bride is at least 18 years old and the groom is at least 21 years old as legally required under Indian law.
steps.calloutText: Marriages already solemnized by religious customs fall under the Hindu Marriage Act. Civil weddings fall under the Special Marriage Act.

steps.title: Log In to State Marriage Registration Portal
steps.description: Create an account on the state marriage registration portal and select 'Register Marriage' under registration services.
steps.where: Official State Registration Portal (e.g. e-Nagar / IGR Portal)

steps.title: Fill Bride and Groom Personal and Family Details
steps.description: Enter full legal names, dates of birth, religion, father's names, mother's names, and present addresses of both parties.

steps.title: Fill Date, Venue, and Solemnization Ritual Details
steps.description: Provide the exact wedding date, venue address, priest or solemnizer details, and select the applicable marriage act.
steps.calloutText: You can apply at the Sub-Registrar Office where the wedding took place or where either spouse resided for six months.

steps.title: Enter Details of Witnesses and Upload Identity Proofs
steps.description: Enter the names, addresses, and Aadhaar numbers of at least two adult witnesses who were present at the wedding.
steps.calloutText: Witnesses must be aged 18 or older and must possess valid government identity proof such as Aadhaar or Passport.

steps.title: Upload Joint Photographs, Wedding Card, and Age Proofs
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of wedding card, joint couple photo, age proofs, and witness ID cards in PDF format under 2 MB.

steps.title: Pay Statutory Government Registration Fee Online
steps.description: Pay the nominal statutory government registration fee of ₹5 to ₹100 online and download the payment receipt.
steps.where: State Treasury Cyber Treasury / Online Payment Gateway

steps.title: Physical Verification at Sub-Registrar Office and Certificate Delivery
steps.description: Both spouses and two witnesses appear before the Sub-Registrar for signature verification. Collect the embossed marriage certificate.

documentRequirements.name: Proof of Age for Bride and Groom
documentRequirements.description: Birth certificate, 10th school mark sheet, passport, or driving licence proving bride is 18+ and groom is 21+.

documentRequirements.name: Proof of Present Residence for Both Parties
documentRequirements.description: Aadhaar card, voter ID, passport, or utility bill confirming continuous residence within the Sub-Registrar jurisdiction.

documentRequirements.name: Wedding Invitation Card or Solemnization Certificate
documentRequirements.description: Original printed wedding card, temple/gurdwara solemnization certificate, or church marriage register copy.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Original invitation card or priest certificate

documentRequirements.name: Joint Photographs of Husband and Wife
documentRequirements.description: Formal color photographs showing the married couple together along with standard passport-size photos of each.

documentRequirements.name: Identity and Address Proofs of Two Witnesses
documentRequirements.description: Aadhaar cards or voter IDs of at least two adult witnesses who attended the marriage ceremony.

documentRequirements.name: Divorce Decree or Death Certificate of Prior Spouse
documentRequirements.description: Certified court divorce decree or death certificate of previous spouse if either party was married earlier.
documentRequirements.copiesHint: Certified court copy or municipal certificate

rejectionReasons.title: Age Disqualification (Groom Under 21 or Bride Under 18)
rejectionReasons.description: Indian statutory law prohibits registration if the bride is younger than 18 or the groom is younger than 21.
rejectionReasons.solution: Submit genuine proof of age demonstrating both spouses meet legal statutory age limits.

rejectionReasons.title: Submitting Without Prior Spouse Divorce Decree or Death Certificate
rejectionReasons.description: If either party was previously married, failing to produce a certified divorce decree or death certificate halts approval.
rejectionReasons.solution: Attach the authenticated family court divorce decree or prior spouse's municipal death certificate.

rejectionReasons.title: Missing Witness Physical Presence or Incomplete Witness ID Proof
rejectionReasons.description: Witnesses who fail to appear physically before the Sub-Registrar or bring incomplete identity proofs cause application deferral.
rejectionReasons.solution: Ensure at least two adult witnesses accompany the couple to the SRO with original Aadhaar cards.

rejectionReasons.title: Applying Outside Both Parties' Jurisdictional SRO
rejectionReasons.description: Filing with a Sub-Registrar office where neither spouse resided nor the wedding occurred results in jurisdiction rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: File strictly with the SRO where the wedding took place or where either party resided for at least six months.

rejectionReasons.title: Contradictory Names Between Wedding Card and Aadhaar Records
rejectionReasons.description: Major discrepancies between pet names printed on wedding invitations and formal names on Aadhaar trigger rejection.
rejectionReasons.solution: Provide an affidavit clarifying alternate names or use an official temple solemnization certificate with legal names.

rejectionReasons.title: Failure to Appear Within 90 Days of Online Application
rejectionReasons.description: Submitting online but failing to appear at the Sub-Registrar office within the state validity period causes expiry.
rejectionReasons.solution: Book an in-person appointment slot immediately after completing online fee payment.

faqItems.question: Is marriage registration mandatory in India?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The Supreme Court of India mandated compulsory marriage registration across all states to protect spousal rights.

faqItems.question: What is the minimum age for marriage in India?
faqItems.answer: The legal age for marriage is 18 years for the bride and 21 years for the groom under current statutory law.

faqItems.question: What is the statutory government fee to register a marriage?
faqItems.answer: Statutory fees are very nominal, typically ₹5 to ₹100 depending on the state schedule and application timing.

faqItems.question: Within how many days of marriage must we register?
faqItems.answer: Most states require registration within 30 days of the ceremony to avoid delayed late registration surcharges.

faqItems.question: Can a marriage be registered if the wedding occurred years ago?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Marriages can be registered at any time after the wedding by paying the nominal delayed fee.

faqItems.question: What is the difference between registration under Hindu Marriage Act and Special Marriage Act?
faqItems.answer: Hindu Marriage Act registers marriages already solemnized. Special Marriage Act solemnizes civil marriages with a 30-day notice.

faqItems.question: Do witnesses have to appear in person before the Sub-Registrar?
faqItems.answer: Yes. At least two adult witnesses must appear in person before the Sub-Registrar with original identity proofs.

faqItems.question: How can I download my marriage certificate online?
faqItems.answer: Once verified, log in to your state civil portal or DigiLocker, enter your registration number, and download the signed certificate.

GJ.title: How to Register a Marriage in Gujarat (2026)
GJ.summary: In Gujarat, marriages are registered under the Gujarat Compulsory Registration of Marriages Act, 2006 via e-Nagar or local Ward Offices. Learn the 5 rupee timely fee rule, wedding Kankotri proofs, and digital QR certificate issuance.
GJ.verifiedBy: Civic Research Editorial Team - Gujarat Bureau

steps.title: Complete Online Memorandum on Gujarat e-Nagar
steps.description: Log into the e-Nagar portal or visit your municipal ward office to fill the statutory Memorandum of Marriage under the Gujarat 2006 Act.

steps.title: Upload Wedding Invitation Kankotri and Ceremony Photos
steps.description: Attach scanned wedding invitation card (Kankotri), priest solemnization certificate (Gor Maharaj slip), and two photographs of the ceremony.
steps.calloutText: The traditional wedding invitation card in Gujarati or English serves as primary documentary evidence of solemnization.

steps.title: Upload Identity Proofs of Couple and Three Witnesses
steps.description: Upload scanned copies of Aadhaar cards, school leaving certificates for age proof, and identity documents for three adult witnesses.
steps.calloutText: Under Gujarat marriage regulations, three adult witnesses who attended the wedding must sign the register in person.

steps.title: Pay Gujarat Statutory Five Rupee Registration Fee
steps.description: Pay five rupees statutory memorandum fee if applying within 30 days, or applicable delayed fees via Cyber Treasury or cash counter.
steps.where: Gujarat Cyber Treasury / Civic Cash Counter
steps.calloutText: Registering within thirty days costs just five rupees, saving you late penalty surcharges under state rules.

steps.title: Physical Appearance Before Marriage Registrar in Gujarat
steps.description: Visit the municipal ward registrar or rural Talati office with your spouse and three witnesses to sign the official state marriage ledger.
steps.where: Municipal Ward Office or Gram Panchayat Office

steps.title: Download QR-Coded Bilingual Marriage Certificate
steps.description: The Registrar signs the entry. Download your official bilingual certificate in Gujarati and English directly from e-Nagar with QR verification.
steps.calloutText: The digital certificate carries full statutory validity for visa, passport, joint property, and banking formalities.

fees.label: Timely Registration Fee (Within 30 Days)
fees.description: Statutory memorandum fee under Gujarat Compulsory Registration of Marriages Act, 2006.

fees.label: Certified Marriage Certificate Copy Fee
fees.description: Prescribed statutory charge per certified extract under Gujarat state marriage rules.

fees.label: Delayed Registration Late Fee (After 30 Days)
fees.description: Statutory delayed registration surcharge under Section 6 of the Gujarat Marriage Act.

faqItems.question: What is the statutory fee to register a marriage in Gujarat within 30 days?
faqItems.answer: The statutory registration fee is just five rupees under the Gujarat Compulsory Registration of Marriages Act.

faqItems.question: How many witnesses are required for marriage registration in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Three adult witnesses who attended the marriage ceremony must sign the marriage register in person.

faqItems.question: Is the wedding invitation card (Kankotri) accepted as proof in Gujarat?
faqItems.answer: Yes. The wedding invitation card along with priest certificate serves as primary solemnization proof.

faqItems.question: Can I download my Gujarat marriage certificate online?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Once the Registrar approves the entry, download your digitally signed bilingual certificate from e-Nagar.
